claim_text: Peninsula Energy says a cybersecurity incident hit the plant and wellfield operating and control systems at its Lance uranium project
summary: Peninsula Energy says its US subsidiary, Strata Energy, "identified a cybersecurity incident affecting the plant and wellfield operating and control systems at Lance on the morning of Friday, 20 November 2026 (local US time)".
detail: The company calls it a "cybersecurity incident" and a "cyber security incident". Its filings do not use the words attack, hack or ransomware.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The company's own ASX announcement of Nov 25 states it in these words.

claim_text: Peninsula's trading halt request calls it a breach of the company's operating system only
summary: Peninsula's Nov 23 trading halt request says: "the breach was to the Company's operating system only and there was no breach of the Company's administrative systems in USA or Australia."
detail: The filing does not say who caused the breach or how it happened.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The company's own trading halt request to the ASX says it in these words.

claim_text: Operations at Lance are suspended until recovery and checks are finished
summary: Peninsula shut down Lance as a precaution when it found the incident. It says operations "will remain suspended until the necessary recovery and verification program is completed" and it is satisfied they can safely resume.
detail: Peninsula has given no restart date. It says it will give an update on the expected timeline for restarting operations in the coming days.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The Nov 25 ASX announcement says operations remain suspended; The Register reports the same on Nov 26.

claim_text: Peninsula has not said who was behind the incident or how it happened, and is still checking whether data was affected
summary: Peninsula says its investigation is ongoing and that "broader investigations are also focussed on potential data impacts". It has not named a cause or anyone responsible.
detail: The Register notes that Peninsula has not given a restart date and that its investigation, including whether data was compromised, is ongoing.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The Nov 25 announcement says the investigation continues and names no cause; The Register reads it the same way.

claim_text: News outlets describe the incident as a cyberattack
summary: The Register's headline reads "Wyoming uranium operation shuts down after cyberattack", and Cowboy State Daily calls it a "cybersecurity breach".
detail: Both outlets base this on Peninsula's filings. Peninsula itself calls it a cybersecurity incident and has not used the word attack.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Both outlets describe it in these words; neither cites a source besides the company's filings for it being an attack.

claim_text: Peninsula says it notified the relevant US authorities and brought in outside specialists
summary: Peninsula says it "notified relevant authorities in the US and engaged specialist external cyber security consultants, forensic and legal advisers" to help with the investigation, containment and recovery.
detail: The company does not name the authorities it told.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The Nov 25 ASX announcement says it in these words.

claim_text: Wyoming's environmental regulator said it had not been notified as of the morning of Nov 23
summary: A Wyoming Department of Environmental Quality spokesperson told Cowboy State Daily the company had not notified it as of Monday morning, Nov 23. Operators need not report such incidents unless their permit is affected or there is damage.
detail: Cowboy State Daily also reports that the Wyoming Office of Homeland Security said its cyber response team handles incidents like this one. The environmental department said it would look into it.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Cowboy State Daily reports what the agency's spokesperson told it.

claim_text: Peninsula says its corporate and administrative systems were not affected
summary: Peninsula says the incident "appears to be confined to the plant and wellfield operating and control systems". Its corporate systems in the US and Australia, "including payroll and financial administration", remain unaffected.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Both company filings say the administrative systems were not breached.

claim_text: Trading in Peninsula's shares is suspended until Nov 30 at the latest
summary: Peninsula asked for a voluntary suspension of trading in its shares until the earlier of the start of trading on Monday, Nov 30, 2026, or an announcement that operations at Lance have resumed and of any effect on its production guidance.
detail: Before that, it asked for a trading halt on Nov 23.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The two ASX filings set out the halt and the suspension.

claim_text: Peninsula cannot yet say whether the incident will affect its 2027 production guidance
summary: Peninsula says it "is unable to assess whether the incident will materially impact previously stated production guidance for CY2027" and will reassess once operations resume.
detail: The Register reports that Peninsula had withdrawn its 2026 guidance earlier in the year after operational problems at Lance unrelated to this incident.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The Nov 25 announcement says it in these words; The Register adds the earlier guidance history.

claim_text: A Wyoming cybersecurity adviser said the cause could be an outsider or an insider, since the company has said little
summary: A cybersecurity business counselor at CyberWyoming told Cowboy State Daily: "It could be an outsider, it could be an insider... They just said cyber and that operations were down."
detail: This is an outside view on how little the company has said, not evidence of either cause.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Cowboy State Daily quotes the adviser.

claim_text: No link has been shown between the Lance incident and the US outages of the week before
summary: Cowboy State Daily notes that the incident came after a week of high-profile US outages, including the FAA ground stop and problems at Microsoft, Apple and the NSA, and that none of those outages was attributed to a cyberattack.
detail: Peninsula has said nothing about any other incident. The adviser quoted by Cowboy State Daily said there did not appear to be a through line connecting the incidents.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Cowboy State Daily reports this in its own words and quotes the adviser.
